en: Dependent on a state that is both with-protection (*saraṇa*) and subject to taints (*āsava*), a state that is neither with-protection nor subject to taints arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is both with-protection and subject to taints, a state that is without-affliction (*na-araṇa*) and not subject to taints arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both with-protection and subject to taints, states that are both neither with-protection nor subject to taints and without-affliction arise by way of root-condition.
With respect to the root condition, there are three; with respect to the object condition, one … pe … with respect to the non-disappearance condition, three.

Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and without-outflows (*anāsava*), a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and without-outflows arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, one … pe … with respect to the non-disappearance condition, one.

Dependent on a state that is without-conflict (*araṇa*) and with-outflows (*sāsava*), a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and without-outflows arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, one … pe … with respect to the non-disappearance condition, one.

Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and free from taints (*anāsava*), there arises a state that is neither with-conflict nor free from taints by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under the root condition there is one; under the predominance condition there is one …pe… under the non-disappearance condition there is one. (In this manner, it should be expanded in all instances.)
